answer: Escrowed pair scheduling forces every new identity to complete a timed task with an existing one before acting. A zephyr of verification latency means each extra identity must wait out its partner's queue slot, so fake accounts stall on real coordination rather than on fees. An attacker pays the knoll of actual synchronization: N identities need N distinct partners, each consuming scarce calendar capacity that cannot be fabricated. The relic of each completed pairing is a signed timing record, and duplicate or recycled partners void the escrow.
